provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Event family batch. The date check is the whole conversion path. Mid-ticket, so software and AI prices stay below the build. No music, gear or booking brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: First dance, parent dances, grand entrance song, must-play and do-not-play lists, clean edits, and how the DJ reads the dance floor through the night
pageStructurePlus.why: Couples are afraid the music will be wrong or the dance floor empty. Showing the planning process is what makes a DJ feel safe to book.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Grand entrance, toast order, cake cutting, bouquet toss, last dance, checking name pronunciation, and keeping the reception timeline on track
pageStructurePlus.why: Much of the job is the microphone, not the music. Couples and planners pick the entertainer who sounds calm and organised as the emcee.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Uplighting colours, monogram projection, photo booth, cold spark effects where the venue allows, karaoke and late-night party packages
pageStructurePlus.why: Add-ons are where an entertainment company's margin is. Couples add them when they can see them together with prices, not in a later email.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Wireless mics for the officiant and readers, a separate ceremony speaker, processional cues, and outdoor power needs
pageStructurePlus.why: Couples forget the ceremony needs sound until a guest can't hear the vows. A clear ceremony package catches the add-on and the worry.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Homecoming, prom and school dance packages with clean-edit music, company holiday parties, and the insurance and invoice paperwork schools ask for
pageStructurePlus.why: Schools and companies book on paperwork and clean music, not on a wedding reel. A separate page keeps the weekday and off-season calendar full.

designDirections.name: Party Starter
designDirections.bestFor: Mobile DJs doing birthdays, school dances and backyard parties who need a quick date check and clear packages
designDirections.headlineSample: Party and school dance DJ in {City}. Is your date free?
designDirections.whyItFits: Teal and tangerine with warm humanist type feel like a party, and the stacked cards put the three party packages and the date check first.

designDirections.name: Date Check DJ
designDirections.bestFor: Wedding DJs and entertainment companies whose whole funnel is 'is my date free' followed by packages
designDirections.headlineSample: Wedding DJ and emcee in {City}. Check your date.
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo. Poster type reads like a gig flyer, and the ultramarine accent keeps the date check as the loudest thing on the page.

designDirections.name: After Dark
designDirections.bestFor: Multi-DJ entertainment companies selling high-end weddings with lighting, live musicians and late-night packages
designDirections.headlineSample: Wedding entertainment for {City} dance floors that stay full
designDirections.whyItFits: A dark violet page glows like a lit dance floor, and the clean grotesque keeps premium packages and lighting add-ons easy to read.

openers.line: Your Maps listing as a DJ has great reviews but no website, so a couple pricing wedding entertainment in {City} can't see packages or check whether you're free on their Saturday.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The DJ site that would sit behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your bio says to DM for availability. For a wedding DJ, 'is my date free' is the whole first conversation, and couples who have to wait for an answer message the next DJ too.
openers.hook: Read their bio and pinned posts for 'DM for availability' or 'message for rates'. Note the exact wording.
openers.linkLine: A DJ page that answers 'is my date free' on the spot: {demo-link}

openers.line: The DJ site on your listing still shows last year's packages and an uplighting price that may have changed. Couples notice old prices before they notice the dance floor.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale detail: an old year, an old package, a dead form. Note it.
openers.linkLine: The same entertainment company, current and bookable: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Song request PDF on a phone
openers.line: I opened your DJ site on my phone and the music planning form was a PDF I had to download and zoom. Couples plan their first dance and do-not-play list on their phones.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load the planning form or package page on a phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A wedding music planner that works on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to check a wedding date on your site without filling in a long form and waiting. For a DJ, the date is the first question and the easiest one to answer automatically.
openers.hook: Open their contact form and check whether the date is the first field and whether anything answers instantly.
openers.linkLine: A date check that answers before the couple leaves: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Dance floor clips, nowhere to live
openers.line: Your clips of a packed dance floor during the last song are the best proof a DJ can have, and they disappear from the feed in a week. A page of them by venue would keep booking.
openers.hook: Pick one recent dance floor clip and note the venue and the moment. Mention it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your dance floor moments, sorted by venue: {demo-link}

openers.line: One of your reviews says you got every name in the grand entrance right and kept the toasts on time. That's what a nervous couple wants to read about their wedding DJ, right beside the packages.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about the emcee work, the music or the dance floor. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your reviews beside the DJ packages they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Schools start booking homecoming and prom DJs months ahead, and they want clean-edit music and insurance paperwork on a page they can forward to the committee.
openers.hook: Use this in late summer for homecoming and in winter for prom. Check whether they post school dance gigs.
openers.linkLine: A school dance DJ page ready for the committee: {demo-link}

openers.line: Couples send wedding DJ enquiries on Saturday nights while you're behind the decks at someone else's reception. By Monday, some of them have booked whoever replied first.
openers.hook: Look for comments asking 'are you free on' or 'how much for a wedding'. Note one posted on a weekend evening.
openers.linkLine: A DJ page that books the enquiry while you're at a gig: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're bringing on another DJ for next season. Couples booking a multi-DJ company want to see who will actually be at their wedding, and a team page answers that.
openers.hook: Only if they posted about hiring or training a new DJ or emcee. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: An entertainment company site with a DJ team page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You've played receptions at a lot of the well-known venues around {City}, and couples booked at those venues search for a DJ who knows the room.
openers.hook: List two or three venues they've tagged in DJ posts. Name one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: A page for each venue where you've filled the dance floor: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts don't say how the DJ deposit or the final balance works. Couples budgeting for entertainment like to see the retainer and when the rest is due before they reach out.
openers.hook: Look for 'retainer', 'deposit' or 'payment' in their posts or FAQ. Note what they publish and never invent terms.
openers.linkLine: A DJ package page with deposit and balance explained: {demo-link}

openers.line: Venues and schools ask the DJ for an insurance certificate before load-in. A line on the site saying you provide one makes the entertainment company easy to approve.
openers.hook: Check whether they mention insurance or venue requirements anywhere. Never state coverage they haven't published.
openers.linkLine: A DJ site with the venue paperwork answered: {demo-link}

openers.line: It looks like a lot of your wedding gigs come from a few planners and venue coordinators. If one of them moves on, the couples they used to send you need another way to find the DJ.
openers.hook: Look for posts thanking a planner or venue for a referral. Name the relationship if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where a couple would find your DJ work on their own: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} looked like a great party. A packed dance floor like that should be the first thing a couple sees on your DJ site, with the venue named.
openers.hook: Pick their newest posted gig and name it exactly: the venue, the event and the moment on the dance floor.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} looked like a great party.

I looked for a website for {Business Name} and couldn't find a way to check whether you're free on a date without messaging. I put together a sample DJ site with a date check, wedding and party packages and a music planning form, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my message got lost among the date requests. Here's the sample DJ site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It answers 'is my date free' first, then shows packages, uplighting and photo booth add-ons, and a do-not-play list form couples can fill in on a phone. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for DJs and entertainment companies around {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss after a weekend of gigs. Short version: I built a sample DJ site for {Business Name} with a date check, packages and a music planning form, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
 → ask: "How many of your Monday messages are just 'are you free on' a date?"
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting, open dates and package changes. For a DJ business like yours I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Can we walk through it for ten minutes on a weekday afternoon?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and I'll need your packages and booked dates."

objections.objection: I get all my gigs from referrals.
objections.handler: "Referrals are the best gigs. Even referred couples check the DJ online before they reply, and the date check means you don't lose them over the weekend while you're at another wedding."
"Then the date check saves you answering couples for dates you can't take, and the site sells Fridays, Sundays, school dances and company parties instead."

objections.objection: My buddy built me a site a few years ago.
objections.handler: "Keep the domain. The gap is the date check and a music planner that works on a phone. I can rebuild on the address you already have."

objections.objection: I'm on the big wedding listing sites.
objections.handler: "Keep them. Couples who find a DJ there click through to the DJ's own site before they enquire. That's where the date check and packages close it."

objections.objection: Prices depend on the event, I can't post them.
objections.handler: "Post 'from' prices for weddings, parties and school dances, and let add-ons stack on top. Couples want to know if a DJ is in budget before they ask."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a date check, packages and a music planner. One wedding gig covers it."

email.subject: DJ site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for DJs in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name} with a date check and packages. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} DJ demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — school dance committees and newly engaged couples both start booking entertainment after the holidays. Thought of you.

The DJ site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one or two wedding gigs, never to a season. A DJ's tickets are mid-size, so the build has to be too.
The date check is the core of every DJ site. Quote it in the build, never as an add-on.
Price the music planner by how many forms it replaces: first dance, parent dances, do-not-play and timeline.
Add-on menus for uplighting and photo booth are where the DJ's margin is. Price the page to that margin.
Keep monthly add-ons under the cost of one uplighting package.
Sell school dance pages in summer and wedding pushes in late fall.

lineItems.item: Wedding music planner and do-not-play form
lineItems.description: Max with first dance and parent dance picks, grand entrance names with pronunciation, and a printable run of show.

lineItems.item: Add-ons menu with uplighting and photo booth
lineItems.description: Max with colour choices, booth backdrops, cold spark rules by venue and add-on totals shown live.
Max with clean-edit music policy, insurance and invoice paperwork downloads and a committee request form.
Max when each DJ has their own clips, style, reviews and open dates.

lineItems.item: Venue page for a reception venue played
lineItems.description: Max with dance floor clips, load-in notes, power and sound limits at that venue.
Max when packages, the music planner and the date check are all translated, with quinceañera timeline options.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the DJ business
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every weekend's reception or party goes on your Google profile with the venue named, so couples searching for a wedding DJ nearby see you're out every Saturday."

whatElseYouSell.name: Monday-after-the-gig review requests
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The Monday after the wedding, the couple gets a short text asking them to review the DJ while the last song is still in their heads."

whatElseYouSell.name: Dance floor clip posting
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "You send me the phone clips from the party, I cut and post the best dance floor moments with the venue tagged through the week."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, if they film clips but never post them.

whatElseYouSell.name: Bridal show booth with a live date check
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A DJ booth backdrop, a screen running the date check and a card with your add-on menu, so couples at the bridal show hold their date on the spot."
whatElseYouSell.when: Six weeks before their first winter bridal show.

whatElseYouSell.name: School dance mailer to activity directors
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A late-summer note to every high school activity director nearby with the school dance DJ page, clean-music policy and insurance line."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in July, send in August before homecoming planning.

whatElseYouSell.name: Holiday party DJ push to local companies
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A September push to office managers for December party DJs, with a corporate package and open Fridays on one page."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in August, run September and October.

whatElseYouSell.name: Venue coordinator intro packet for the DJ
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page packet for reception venue coordinators: your setup footprint, power needs, insurance line and dance floor clips from their room."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, before venues refresh vendor lists.

whatElseYouSell.name: DJ booth facade and table wrap artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Facade and table wrap artwork with your DJ name and date-check address, so every guest on the dance floor knows who to book."

withoutAI.route: Photo booth operators the DJ partners with
withoutAI.whoPays: The booth operator, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The photo booth company that sets up beside you at receptions books by DM too. Same date-check layout, different add-ons."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Booths and DJs share almost every party and send each other couples.

withoutAI.route: Reception halls the DJ plays every month
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The reception hall you play most months still books from a phone number. Your DJ client can introduce you during load-in."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: DJs know which halls are under-served, and hall owners trust the vendors who keep their dance floor full.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The shop where the DJ rents extra speakers and moving heads takes orders by phone. It needs a catalogue with a date check."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: DJs are their best customers and know the owner. The catalogue logic is one you already understand.

withoutAI.whoPays: The musicians, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The ceremony musicians who hand over to the DJ at cocktail hour book weddings by email. A small date-check site with sample recordings fits them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Ceremony musicians and DJs share the same couples and timelines, and refer to each other.

withoutAI.whoPays: The parent group or school office
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The parent group behind the school dance sells tickets with a cash box. A page for tickets, chaperone sign-ups and the dress code would help."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: The DJ meets the organisers every year, and a small page is an easy budget line.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The quinceañera boutique your families shop at needs a fitting page and a gallery of real celebrations. The DJ plays those parties every month."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Quinceañera vendors refer families to each other constantly, and the DJ is trusted inside that circle.

withAI.route: Print template designer for photo booth operators
withAI.pitchLine: "The couple types their names, date and colours, and the photo booth operator gets print strip designs to approve before the party."
withAI.whyItWorks: Booth operators design a template for every event by hand. It's small, monthly and easy to say yes to.

withAI.route: Reception hall date and capacity assistant
withAI.pitchLine: "Families asking the reception hall about capacity, bar rules or a Saturday in May get answers any hour and a walk-through request."
withAI.whyItWorks: Hall owners miss enquiries while running events. The DJ is in the hall every month to make the intro.

withAI.route: Gear package quote assistant for AV rental shops
withAI.pitchLine: "Someone describes the room and the crowd, and the rental shop gets a suggested speaker, mic and lighting package to quote."
withAI.whyItWorks: AV shops field vague requests all day. The DJ client knows the owner and the gear.

withAI.pitchLine: "Couples describe their style, and the ceremony musicians get a processional and recessional shortlist from their own repertoire."
withAI.whyItWorks: Musicians answer 'what should we walk down to' for every wedding. Small, cheap and useful.

withAI.route: Dance ticket and chaperone assistant for school groups
withAI.pitchLine: "Parents and students ask about tickets, guest passes and the dress code, and chaperones pick shifts, without one volunteer answering everything."
withAI.whyItWorks: Volunteer organisers are swamped before every dance. The DJ sees it happen each year.

withAI.route: Court-of-honour scheduling assistant for quinceañera boutiques
withAI.pitchLine: "Families the DJ meets at quinceañera parties book fittings for the birthday girl and her whole court in one go, in English or Spanish, with reminders before each visit."
withAI.whyItWorks: Group fittings are the boutique's biggest scheduling headache, and the DJ client is trusted in that community.

softwareAI.name: Instant date-check reply with DJ packages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A couple who checks a wedding date gets 'yes, it's open' with your packages and a call link straight away, even while you're at a reception."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build. Needs the booked dates and the package guide.

softwareAI.name: DJ contract and deposit signing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Couples sign the entertainment agreement and pay the deposit in one link, so the party date is held the night they decide."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 1. Needs their contract, reviewed by their own attorney, and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Wedding DJ question answerer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'Do you do ceremony sound', 'how much is uplighting' and 'are you free in June' get answered from your real packages and calendar."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs packages, add-ons and calendar access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Add-on checkout for uplighting and photo booth
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Booked couples add uplighting, a photo booth or cold sparks from their phone and pay for them, without another email to the DJ."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the add-on prices and venue rules for each effect.

softwareAI.name: Balance-due reminders before the gig
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Two weeks before the party, the client gets the balance link, so nobody hands the DJ an envelope during the reception."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the payment terms per booking.

softwareAI.name: Couple planning portal with run of show
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Couples build the reception timeline, entrance order and special dances in one place, and the DJ prints the run of show the night before."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their planning questions and timeline template.

softwareAI.name: Playlist draft from the couple's favourites
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Couples list a few songs they love and their crowd's ages, and the DJ gets a dance floor set draft that respects the do-not-play list."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their music library categories. The DJ always decides the set. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Name pronunciation recorder for the grand entrance
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The wedding party records how to say each name, so the emcee gets every grand entrance right."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the planning form and a way to share recordings.

softwareAI.name: Gig-night phone answerer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "While you're announcing the first dance, a caller asking about entertainment for June hears your open dates and gets a call booked for Monday."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, before engagement season. Needs packages, calendar and escalation rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Gear load list for each party
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each booking prints the gear it needs: ceremony speaker, wireless mics, uplights, booth, so nothing is left in the garage before a wedding."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their gear list and which packages use what.

softwareAI.name: Dance floor clip captions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Post a dance floor clip and a caption tagging the venue and naming the song moment is ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs past captions and vendor tags. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Wedding DJ review replies
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a couple reviews their reception music, a reply naming their venue and their last song is drafted for you to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: School dance paperwork pack
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Schools download the dance contract, the clean-music policy, vendor tax forms and an insurance certificate request from one page."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, before homecoming. Needs their school contract and policies.

softwareAI.name: Friend referral ask after the wedding
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A month after the wedding, the couple gets a note asking if any friends just got engaged, with the DJ date check to share."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs past wedding dates and contacts.

softwareAI.name: Add-on suggestions by venue and guest count
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For each booked wedding, the DJ sees which add-ons suit the venue and crowd, like ceremony sound for a lawn or uplighting for a dark hall."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs venue notes and add-on rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Reception timeline drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the ceremony time and dinner style, and the couple gets a reception timeline draft with entrances, toasts and dances for the DJ to adjust."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the DJ's standard timelines. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Multi-DJ gig assignment calendar
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Assign each wedding and party to a DJ, track who has which gear, and let couples see who their DJ will be."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once they run a second DJ. Needs the DJ roster and pay rules.

softwareAI.name: DJ pay and gig payout tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each DJ on the team sees their gigs, add-on bonuses and what they're owed after every party weekend."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7, for multi-DJ companies. Needs pay rules per gig type.

softwareAI.name: Final-details reminder the week before
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A week out, the couple is reminded to finish the music planner and entrance names, so the DJ isn't chasing them the night before."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the planning portal and booking dates.

softwareAI.name: Emcee method answers for new DJs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New DJs ask how the owner runs a grand entrance, handles a drunk toast or fills an empty dance floor, and get the owner's own answer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, when training new DJs. Needs the owner's notes and approval of every answer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the date check for mobile DJs
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a date check, add-on checkout and music planner for one wedding DJ. Every mobile DJ answers 'are you free' by hand on Mondays."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Mobile DJs are many, talk in groups and share the exact same funnel.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Member template for a DJ association chapter
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Chapter members who spin weddings get a ready site with the reception date check and add-on menu, paid for once by the chapter."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: DJ chapters meet regularly and need renewal reasons. One agreement reaches a room of buyers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each entertainer on the roster gets a profile with clips and open party dates under the company's one booking flow."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Multi-op companies grow by adding DJs. Every new entertainer is another page.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency gets DJ clients and builds a brochure. License my entertainment template with the date check and add-on checkout working."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the booking logic.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Photo booth businesses across the region
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Each booth business, at your normal rate
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Booth companies have the same party date check and add-on menu problem. The DJ template becomes a booth template in a day."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Same buyers, same weekends and the same funnel.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Site kit for a DJ training school
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your graduates can mix but can't book a wedding. A ready DJ site kit makes your course worth more."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Courses sell outcomes, and a booking site is the outcome students want.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: DJ directory for a pro audio retailer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The audio shop every local DJ buys speakers from could list them for party hosts who walk in asking for a DJ."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Retailers want loyal pro customers. Sending them gigs keeps them buying.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Each host, at your normal rate
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Karaoke and trivia hosts book private parties the same way a DJ does. The party package page carries over."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Often the same people, with the same weekend calendar problem.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every franchise owner gets a local page listing their entertainers, open party Saturdays and booth add-ons, all from one shared build."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many territories on the same template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A band agency with many acts needs the same date check per act and an add-on menu for ceremony and cocktail-hour music."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies book many acts on many dates. The DJ date check scales to a roster.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Couples book a DJ who can load in that afternoon, so a wedding DJ an hour outside {City} never competes with the one I built for."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Reception gigs are local, so the template and proof travel without conflict.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Fix DJ sites with broken booking forms
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your wedding DJ request form stopped sending months ago. I can rebuild it so the dance floor bookings land again."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These DJs already paid once and know what a broken form costs them.

upsellLadder.offer: DJ site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The DJ site and the care plan go on one contract, so a newly booked Saturday or a package change is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a couple who said yes and then booked another DJ before paying.
upsellLadder.line: "That couple would have signed and paid the DJ deposit the same night."

upsellLadder.trigger: A couple sends a thank-you message after a packed dance floor.
upsellLadder.line: "That couple loved the party. Let's ask them for the review on Monday."

upsellLadder.offer: Add-on checkout for uplighting and photo booth
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of form data show couples asking about uplighting or the booth after booking.
upsellLadder.line: "Booked couples keep asking about uplighting. Let them add it and pay from the wedding planner."

upsellLadder.offer: Couple planning portal with run of show
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention chasing a couple for their first dance song the week of the wedding.
upsellLadder.line: "The first dance song arrives weeks early when the reception planner asks for it."

upsellLadder.offer: School dance mailer to activity directors
upsellLadder.trigger: Their autumn calendar has open Fridays and they mention a school dance they enjoyed.
upsellLadder.line: "Your open Fridays are homecoming dances. Let's tell every activity director nearby."

upsellLadder.trigger: They turn away a wedding date or bring on a second DJ.
upsellLadder.line: "The wedding date you turned away could go to your second DJ under your name."
